newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin defends one-day military training.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin defends one-day military training.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Friday defended plans to cut a post-conscription introduction to the military for young people to just one day, saying a longer course would be too expensive.

Right-wing opposition parties denounced the Socialist-led government's scheme, unveiled on Thursday, to abandon a planned five-day introduction to the armed forces and call up all young people for just a single day before their 18th birthday.

Jospin, who came to power last month, said the government was not challenging Chirac's decision to phase out conscription, a mainstay of French defence policy since the 1789 Revolution, and shift to an all-professional forces by 2002.
"The choice of the professional army has been taken by the president. We haven't questioned his choice," Jospin told Radio Luxembourg in a rare interview.

"These five days would be very expensive and there would be problems for the armed forces to organise it," Jospin said. Young people would be lectured on patriotism and given an insight into job opportunities in the military.

The five-day plan was a brainchild of former defence minister Charles Millon who wanted to keep a link between the armed forces and the public at large as France phases out compulsory national service by 2002.
Francois Fillon, a defence expert in Chirac's conservative RPR party, denounced the watered-down Socialist plan, part of defence savings after the Cold War.
"This is a rushed, contradictory and useless decision," he said.
